question.title: Statewide Referendum A - Homestead Exemption For Certain Municipal Corporations

source.name: Georgia General Assembly, HB 820 (2017-2018 Regular Session), Senate Committee on Finance substitute LC 44 0861S (PDF at legis.ga.gov)

ballot_text.source_title: HB 820, 'A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT ... a new homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes'; its ballot words begin 'Do you approve a new homestead exemption in a municipal corporation that is located in more than one county ...'. The source does not print the label 'Statewide Referendum A'; the match to ours is by subject and date (see why/notes).
ballot_text.type_quote: purpose of submitting this Act to the electors of the entire state for approval or rejection. The

fact.quote: (a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in this Constitution, no property shall be exempted from ad valorem taxation unless the exemption is approved by two-thirds of the members elected to each branch of the General Assembly in a roll-call vote and by a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon.
fact.why: Kind: a statewide referendum on a general Act (HB 820, enacted as Act 346 per the legislature's annual summary: 'Effective May 3, 2018, and subject to a statewide referendum.'), held 'on November 6, 2018'. The Act's Section 2 cites Art. VII, Sec. II, Para. II(a)(1) of the Georgia Constitution, and that paragraph (legislature's annotated Constitution, 2016 edition, quoted) requires approval by two-thirds of each house and 'a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon'. The Act's own Section 3 says the same in votes cast: 'If more than one-half of the votes cast on such question are for approval of the Act' (the sentence runs on to the next numbered line, so only the single-line part is quoted in the act field). Share needed = more than one-half of the votes cast on the question = 0.5. Caveats: the text saved is the Senate Finance substitute, not the final enrolled Act (the legislature's summary of Act 346 describes the same 'municipal purposes' exemption); the Constitution text is the 2016 edition.

source.name: Georgia General Assembly (Legislative Counsel), Constitution of the State of Georgia, annotated edition (2016) - Art. VII, Sec. II, Para. II(a)(1), at legis.ga.gov document library (2ga-const-(v2)-2016-pdf.pdf); NOT the current text: the SOS's current edition could not be read

fact.note: the reader gave the share the referendum needs (0.5); D3 records it as the case of Ga. Const. art. VII, s.II, para.II(a)(1) holding: an Act exempting property from ad valorem taxation, which needs 'a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon' (data/measure/thresholds.json)

threshold.rule: a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon
threshold.quote: (a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in this Constitution, no property shall be exempted from ad valorem taxation unless the exemption is approved by two-thirds of the members elected to each branch of the General Assembly in a roll-call vote and by a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon.
threshold.read_in: step (a), with the ballot texts (data/measure/ballot-texts.json); each such Act's own section 3 says the same in votes cast: 'If more than one-half of the votes cast on ... such question are for approval of the Act' (HB 820 of 2018, HB 808 of 2024, as saved; the gap is the bill's line number or page break)

question.title: Statewide Referendum B - Tax Exemption For Homes For The Mentally Disabled

source.name: Georgia General Assembly (Legislative Counsel), Summary of General Statutes Enacted at the 1st Session of the 154th General Assembly (2017), entry 'Act 25; HB 196'

ballot_text.source_title: Act 25; HB 196 (2017), Section 2: exemption for 'nonprofit homes for the mentally disabled' subject to a state-wide referendum. The source does not print 'Statewide Referendum B' or a ballot date; the match to ours is by subject (see why/notes).
ballot_text.type_quote: Subject to approval in a state-wide referendum, Section 2 of the Act expands the ad valorem tax exemption for nonprofit homes for the mentally disabled

fact.quote: Effective July 1, 2017, except Section 2 which shall become effective on January 1, 2019, if passed by a majority of voters in a state-wide referendum.
fact.why: Kind: a statewide referendum on a section of a general Act (Act 25, HB 196 of 2017, Section 2), which takes effect on January 1, 2019 only 'if passed by a majority of voters in a state-wide referendum'. A majority of the voters in the referendum = more than one-half of the votes cast = 0.5. The constitutional provision is not named in the summary; it reads as Art. VII, Sec. II, Para. II(a)(1) (an exemption from ad valorem taxation needs two-thirds of each house and 'a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon', quoted in the also field from the legislature's 2016 annotated Constitution). INFERRED parts: that this Act falls under Para. II(a)(1), that 'majority of voters' means of those voting, and that it is the question we call Referendum B (the Act's own text and ballot words were not obtained: the legislature's bill page is script-driven and sos.ga.gov refused us; the Act 25 text was not found by any address I could use).

source.name: Georgia General Assembly (Legislative Counsel), Summary of General Statutes Enacted at the 1st Session of the 154th General Assembly (2017), entry 'Act 25; HB 196'

fact.note: held: the orchestrator's word of 2026-11-07 14:21 ('For 2018 B, read its ballot text. If the text shows it exempts property from ad valorem tax, the constitution governs it and it is stated. If the text doesn't show that, hold it. Reason: the 1/2 must come from the law, and only the kind of act may be read from the ballot.'). Its ballot text and the Act's own text were not read: the legislature's bill page is built by script and gives no text (legis.ga.gov/legislation/69712, read 14:21 UTC), and sos.ga.gov refused (HTTP 403). The Legislative Counsel's summary of Act 25 (quoted) says Section 2 'expands the ad valorem tax exemption for nonprofit homes for the mentally disabled', but it is not the ballot text
